decisionRule: Accept only an exact-source one-time comparison or coined image with no bounded reusable target. Reject if the wording is an ordinary reusable construction, a plausible prior-owner sense, or an exact duplicate that must follow its owner row. Rejection retains editorial hold; it does not approve an alias or new lesson.

rows.exactExpression: tension hanging there like a cloud
rows.exactSourceSentence: The silence left tension hanging there like a cloud.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Unresolved discomfort remains present; a weather simile.
rows.reason: The sentence explicitly compares the remaining silence/tension to a cloud. “Hanging there like a cloud” is a tailored image; removing the cloud loses this source-specific comparison.

rows.exactExpression: show the touch of the hand
rows.exactSourceSentence: Handmade seals show the touch of the hand.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Reveal human craftsmanship; a touch metaphor.
rows.reason: “Show the touch of the hand” describes the visual evidence of handmaking on these seals, but the exact wording is not a stable expression distinct from ordinary “handmade” or “human touch”.

rows.exactExpression: pieces of heritage made tangible
rows.exactSourceSentence: These garments are pieces of heritage made tangible.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Cultural tradition given a physical form; a material metaphor.
rows.reason: “Made tangible” is a natural reusable result construction: garments make an abstract heritage visible or touchable. The source can remain held pending a seven-step/value test; it is not merely a one-off comparison.

rows.exactExpression: feeds the memory
rows.exactSourceSentence: Traditional craft feeds the memory of a community.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Sustains cultural recollection; a food metaphor.
rows.reason: Traditional craft “feeds the memory” personifies memory as something nourished. This unusual craft-and-memory image has no bounded transferable construction in the source.

rows.exactExpression: carry the fingerprints of a culture
rows.exactSourceSentence: Local ceramics carry the fingerprints of a culture.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Show a culture's distinctive mark; a fingerprint metaphor.
rows.reason: “Fingerprints of a culture” uses a reusable distinctive-mark metaphor. Earlier owners 1562 (own fingerprint on a cup) and 1937 (clear fingerprint) establish nearby teaching territory; compare sense and grammar before exclusion.

rows.exactExpression: cultural fingerprints
rows.exactSourceSentence: Local crafts are cultural fingerprints worth preserving.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Distinctive signs of a community's identity; a fingerprint metaphor.
rows.reason: “Cultural fingerprints” is a compact, potentially reusable noun metaphor and repeats 4457’s craft/identity situation. Resolve the pair together against fingerprint owners 1562/1937 rather than excluding the duplicate alone.

rows.exactExpression: rarely arrive unchanged
rows.exactSourceSentence: Shared traditions rarely arrive unchanged.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Typically evolve when moving between cultures; a travel metaphor.
rows.reason: “Rarely arrive unchanged” is ordinary reusable change/arrival language for traditions, not a one-time comparison. Low independent lesson value may justify hold, but does not satisfy the one-off-image exclusion rule.

rows.exactExpression: made with a bit more soul
rows.exactSourceSentence: The handmade chair felt made with a bit more soul.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Made with more care and character; a soul metaphor.
rows.reason: “A bit more soul” is a reusable warmth/character expression, close to existing owner1533 “a little more soul” and owner1619 for homes. Need a bounded owner comparison for a handmade chair.

rows.exactExpression: win on character
rows.exactSourceSentence: Antique furniture can win on character.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Compare more favorably in personality or aesthetic quality; a competition metaphor.
rows.reason: “Win on character” is a potentially reusable evaluative collocation for antiques. Existing owner3393 teaches “full of character” in distinctive appealing settings; establish whether the competitive “win on” syntax merits an owner extension or hold.

rows.exactExpression: traditions are a bit like roots
rows.exactSourceSentence: Traditions are a bit like roots for a community.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Customs give a culture stability and connection to its past; a plant metaphor.
rows.reason: The sentence openly marks the roots analogy, but roots-for-community is productive and appears in existing roots owners 1471/1481. It is not safe to discard without owner-sense/grammar review.

rows.exactExpression: the wheels are still turning, but the thinking behind them has shifted
rows.exactSourceSentence: The wheels are still turning, but the thinking behind them has shifted with climate concerns.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Transport continues while attitudes to it change; a wheel metaphor.
rows.reason: The whole wheels-still-turning/thinking-has-shifted transport contrast is assembled for climate concerns. No one bounded fixed unit preserves both parts of this sentence.

rows.exactExpression: the mother of better transport
rows.exactSourceSentence: Urban congestion can be the mother of better transport.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: A problem that stimulates innovation; a parentage metaphor.
rows.reason: “Mother of better transport” adapts the “necessity is the mother of invention” proverb specifically to congestion. The source is a one-time proverb variation, not a natural standalone target.

rows.exactExpression: the same bones, but it moves to a different rhythm
rows.exactSourceSentence: The network may have the same bones, but it moves to a different rhythm after the update.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: The system's basic form remains while how it operates changes; body and music metaphors.
rows.reason: Same bones/different rhythm combines two images to characterize this network update. The full sentence is an extended one-off comparison rather than one stable expression.

rows.exactExpression: first instinct rather than their last option
rows.exactSourceSentence: The city wants buses to be the first instinct rather than their last option.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: A preferred automatic choice instead of a reluctant fallback; a contrast metaphor.
rows.reason: “First instinct” and “last option” are natural reusable choice terms. The bus-promotion contrast also recurs verbatim at 4572 and is near owner4511 “default choice”; resolve paired source/owner treatment before excluding.

rows.exactExpression: smarter in the hand
rows.exactSourceSentence: With live updates, transport becomes smarter in the hand.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: More useful through phone-based tools; a hand metaphor.
rows.reason: “Smarter in the hand” is coined for phone-held live transport updates. The exact phrase lacks a clear reusable meaning without this device context.

rows.exactExpression: first instinct rather than their last option
rows.exactSourceSentence: The city wants buses to be the first instinct rather than their last option.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: A preferred automatic choice instead of a reluctant fallback; a contrast metaphor.
rows.reason: Exact repeat of 4557’s bus “first instinct/last option” sentence. A duplicate must follow the eventual 4557 owner or hold disposition, not be excluded independently as if unrelated.

rows.exactExpression: roads would start to breathe
rows.exactSourceSentence: With fewer cars, the roads would start to breathe.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Congestion would ease; a breathing metaphor.
rows.reason: Roads beginning to breathe personifies reduced traffic, close to existing owner591 “the whole city breathes more easily” in urban relief. Its actor and grammar differ, so a bounded same-sense review is needed before exclusion.

rows.exactExpression: the choice starts to make itself
rows.exactSourceSentence: With only two days off, the choice starts to make itself.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: One option becomes so attractive that deciding feels automatic; a personification.
rows.reason: “The choice starts to make itself” is a potentially transferable obvious-decision personification. Prior source-specific assessment retained it on hold for missing alternatives/criteria, not as an approved one-off exclusion; preserve that gate.

rows.exactExpression: pass through people's lives
rows.exactSourceSentence: Progress on a map must pass through people's lives.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Affect residents directly during implementation; a journey metaphor.
rows.reason: Progress on a map “passing through people’s lives” is a crafted map-versus-lived-impact maxim for transport. Neither half alone preserves this source argument as a bounded lexical target.

rows.exactExpression: the mental baggage sometimes comes along for the ride
rows.exactSourceSentence: On a short local trip, the mental baggage sometimes comes along for the ride.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Everyday concerns persist during travel; a luggage metaphor.
rows.reason: “Mental baggage” and “come along for the ride” are separately reusable expressions; the travel sentence puns on their joint use. Excluding the entire sentence would silently discard two plausible target/owner routes.

rows.exactExpression: looked at life through one window
rows.exactSourceSentence: Before travelling, she had looked at life through one window.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Seen life from only one perspective; a window metaphor.
rows.reason: Looking at life through one window is a one-time single-window image for this traveller’s previously limited perspective; the exact image is not established as a bounded expression.

rows.exactExpression: a nature trip in disguise
rows.exactSourceSentence: The island break felt like a nature trip in disguise.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: An urban trip that unexpectedly includes nature; a disguise metaphor.
rows.reason: “X in disguise” is a productive reusable reclassification construction; “nature trip in disguise” has a clear trip-type meaning. Existing “blessing in disguise” owner106 is different, so keep for course-value/grammar review rather than exclude.

rows.exactExpression: doesn't put all its beauty in one basket
rows.exactSourceSentence: The region doesn't put all its beauty in one basket.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Has beauty in several kinds of places; an adaptation of a fixed basket idiom.
rows.reason: “Doesn’t put all its beauty in one basket” is a source-specific substitution into the fixed eggs-in-one-basket idiom. Beauty is not a natural fixed target; the adapted sentence is a one-time comparison.

rows.exactExpression: offer not just convenience, but also soul
rows.exactSourceSentence: A destination should offer not just convenience, but also soul.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Provide practical ease and distinctive human character; a soul metaphor.
rows.reason: The destination’s convenience-versus-soul comparison is custom rhetoric for tourism. “Offer not just X but Y” is ordinary syntax and “soul” alone would be a different broad target.

rows.exactExpression: a restful hotel is golden
rows.exactSourceSentence: After a long flight, a restful hotel is golden.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Good sleep is exceptionally valuable; a gold metaphor.
rows.reason: Predicative “is golden” naturally means particularly valuable or welcome; the hotel is one instance of that reusable evaluative construction. Hold pending naturalness/owner review, not exclusion.

rows.exactExpression: plugged into the pulse of the city
rows.exactSourceSentence: The station hotel feels plugged into the pulse of the city.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Closely connected to urban activity; an electrical and heartbeat metaphor.
rows.reason: “Plugged into” and “pulse of the city” are reusable connection/vitality metaphors; existing pulse owners 338/1058 give nearby teaching territory. The combined hotel phrase needs a bounded owner/sense review, not one-off disposal.

rows.exactExpression: half the holiday
rows.exactSourceSentence: At a resort, the hotel can become half the holiday.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: A major part of the vacation experience; a part-whole metaphor.
rows.reason: “The hotel can become half the holiday” is a source-specific resort-value comparison, not the fixed “half the battle” idiom or a stable half-the-holiday target.
